1	# Rung N (`rung-nat-checker`): the judge's ruling on the first refusal
2	
3	**Decision: repair.** The skeptic is right on both grounds of its refusal: two repairs this rung makes have no gated assertion. The repair round adds one test and re-pins another, and shows each red without its edit. It gives the skeptic's measured defects their homes and corrects the report and the record. No source file under `ProjectFortress/src/` changes in this round, and decision 3 stands as landed. It goes to Pavol as the rung's own reading of his rule, which is what it is.
4	
5	Read for this ruling: the net diff `47437c65f...eb72cf0a9`, `REPORT.md`, `record.md`, `SKEPTIC.md`, the skeptic's captures cited below, the specification passages below (each read at least ten lines either side), `explorations/reviews/array-design-review.md:75-82` and `:175-183`, `explorations/reviews/nat-checking-plan.md:340-430`, `explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47`, `:92-93` and `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:108-131`. Nothing was built or run for this ruling.
6	
7	## 1. The two refusal grounds: the skeptic is right on both
8	
9	**(a) The `ExportChecker` repair has no test.** The edit turns `equalIntExprs` from the constant `false` into `Formula.nEq` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:645-646`). The skeptic's one-file A/B shows it is load-bearing: with only that file at `47437c65f`, a component that exports its own sized api is refused with "Missing declarations: {unbox[\nat k\]...}", and with the edit it checks clean (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/skeptic/export-ab.txt:3-11`). With the edit the component also compiles, and so does its user (`probes/skeptic/differential-2.txt:181-186`). The specification settles the case: "A component must include, for every API A it exports, matching definitions for all the declarations in A ... The header and type of d' must be the same as the header and type of d" (`Specification/basic/components/apis.tex:250-256`). A sized declaration that matches must therefore pass. That makes this a repair by the rung and home 1. REPORT.md does list the edit (`REPORT.md:29`), but its defect-home table has no row for it (`REPORT.md:114-130`), and no test runs the export check on a sized api.
10	
11	**(b) The use-site arithmetic check is not pinned.** `XXXNatArithChecker.test:3` matches `Arithmetic on nat static arguments is not supported by the type checker`. That sentence is the shared suffix of two errors: the declared-type check (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:107-108`) and the use-site check (`:144-145`). Both appear in the run (`probes/skeptic/junit-rerun.txt:101-102`, `:107-108`). Delete `:144-145` and the declared-type error still carries the string, so the test stays green. REPORT.md counts the use-site repair as home 1 with this test (`REPORT.md:123`), and that claim is false until the test is pinned. The harness checks a `_contains` and a `_WIcontains` key on the same stream independently (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:147-161`), so the test can pin both the error count, as `XXXNatRetSizeChecker.test:3` and `XXXNatMismatchChecker.test:3` already do, and the use-site message.
12	
13	## 2. The skeptic's other corrections
14	
15	1. **Decision 3 needs three additions. The skeptic is right on all three, and it misses a fourth point.**
16	   - (a) In an overload set, an arm whose size is dead is dropped from static resolution, and run-time dispatch still selects it (`probes/skeptic/dead-arms.txt:44-55`, `:74-95`).
17	   - (b) A dead type parameter passes, because `killIvars` turns it into `BOTTOM` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:1937-1940`). A dead size is refused (`dead-arms.txt:7-12` against `:34-41`). So sizes are stricter than types, and the report does not say so.
18	   - (c) E2, the rule Pavol took, is written as "the interpreter's `BottomType` rule ... the six declarations pass because their dead parameters reach nothing" (`explorations/reviews/array-design-review.md:181`; the reasoning is at `:81`). The interpreter runs a call to a function with a dead size. So reading "reaches a name" as covering every call's static arguments is the rung's own decision. REPORT.md calls it "Pavol's rule" (`REPORT.md:89`, `:155`), which overstates it.
19	   - The point the skeptic missed: every overload shape it used for (a) and (b) mixes a generic declaration with a non-generic one. The shapes are `dd[\nat n\](x: Any)` beside `dd(x: ZZ32)`, `ee[\nat n\](x: ZZ32)` beside `ee(x: Any)`, and `SkBoolArm`'s pair. The committed specification refuses each such pair at the declaration: "it is an error for their static parameters to differ ..., or for one declaration to have static parameters and another to not have them" (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-107`; the same rule is at `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:95-103`). That sentence is Pavol's open decision. This rung "neither enforces it nor relaxes it further", and the size-generic arm beside a less specific sibling is the one shape it admits (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:127`). So `SkDeadTop` and `SkDeadVal` are accepted under the exception Pavol granted. They are not a new acceptance by this rung, and their fate follows his decision on that sentence. The record has to say so.
20	2. **The literal-sizes sentence in section 11 (`REPORT.md:176`) is wrong as written. The skeptic is right.** A generic trait is refused (`probes/skeptic/differential-3.txt:13-19`). An object is accepted through `checkO` (`differential-1.txt:130-137`). The type twin on a trait is accepted and its compiled run prints 3 and 4 (`differential-3.txt:35-52`). The cause is `checkP`, which compares `STypeArg` pairs and nothing else, under the team's "Todo: Handle int, nat, bool args" (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:455-468`, `:460`).
21	3. **A failure-mode account is owed. The skeptic is right.** Every crash the rung replaces now has a new behaviour, and REPORT.md describes none of them. The skeptic's list (`SKEPTIC.md` section 10) is accurate as far as I checked. `unsupportedKindError` throws (`STypesUtil.scala:565-567`), placed at the declaration's parameter (`differential-1.txt:278-281`), and the thrown error hides the component's other errors (`differential-1.txt:302-305` against `bool-control.txt:13-18`).
22	4. **Provisional row 388's method half duplicates ledger row 21. The skeptic is right.** Row 21 reads "static arguments on a generic *method* cannot be inferred" (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:135`), from a walk probe. The rung's precedent search did not look at the ledger.
23	5. **The row 387 bullet for Pavol (`record.md:65`) needs to cover sizes. The skeptic is right.** `keep-size-params` makes sizes reach the same acceptance (`REPORT.md:65`, the `SubOvSwap` row).
24	6. **Section 12 timings (`REPORT.md:181`). The skeptic is right.** The text says "three times" and then lists four durations, with no machine line. `explorations/protocol.md:192-193` requires the machine line.
25	
26	## 3. The skeptic's recommended rows, and the home each takes
27	
28	The three-homes rule of the brief applies to every defect anyone measured in this rung, the skeptic included. Here the skeptic is wrong in two places. It gave a defect the specification settles a row only, where an expected-failure test can be written. And it did not check its overload shapes against the static-parameter sentence.
29	
30	- **A numeral argument at a generic call whose static arguments are inferred** (`SkLitArgN`, `SkLitArgT`). Measured: the inferred call is refused as "not applicable to ... IntLiteral", while the written-out call and the non-generic call pass. The types case was refused the same way before the edit (`differential-3.txt:55-99`), and walk prints 6 for every form. The specification settles it. Numerals have their own types and convert by the library's coercions (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:127-144`), and a coercion occurs at "arguments to functionals and constructors where the corresponding parameters have declared types" (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:98-103`; the skeptic's `:101-102` is one line off). Neither form is an overload, so the static-parameter sentence does not apply. The repair is in static-argument inference with coercion, and it is outside this rung's charter: the defect predates the rung for types. The compile command fails today, so an `XXX` test can be written. **Home 2**: an expected-failure test and a provisional row. The skeptic's "fourth case, row only" is wrong. The fourth case is for a repair outside the rung's scope, and the brief's three-homes rule still gives a defect the specification settles a gated `XXX` test whenever the failing command allows one. The rung itself argued that only a *succeeding* command rules the test out (`REPORT.md:128`).
31	- **`checkP` has no size case** (`SkLitTrait` refused, `SkLitTraitT` accepted). The committed prose states no multiple-instantiation exclusion. My grep of `Specification/basic/` and `advanced/` finds none, and the relations are "the smallest ones that satisfy all the properties given" (`Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:184-189`). So refusing `SkLitTrait` conforms to the committed specification. The type twin's acceptance is route A, the checker's rule that Pavol decided to keep (`explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:92`), and rung S of this batch revises the prose. Adding the size case now would accept a program the committed prose refuses, which is a stop of this batch. The plan left it out on purpose (`explorations/reviews/nat-checking-plan.md:376-384`). **Recorded, not repaired**: a provisional row naming the few lines in `cP` that become owed once the route-A revision lands. It is not a defect against today's specification, so it takes no `XXX` test.
32	- **A dead-size arm in an overload set** (`SkDeadTop`, `SkDeadVal`). Compiled, `SkDeadTop` prints 1 and 2, the same as walk (`dead-arms.txt:44-55`), so the only failure is `SkDeadVal`. The checker accepts it, and the compiled run dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: SkDeadVal$n`, while walk dies with "undefined variable [n]" (`dead-arms.txt:74-95`). The specification is silent on inference (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:15`; `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:137-138`), and the pair is one the static-parameter sentence refuses (section 2, item 1). **Home 3**: the probes are already committed under `probes/skeptic/`, plus a provisional row. One more probe is needed to find the fix's location: the same program with the size written out. It separates the unknown size from the value-position gap that belongs to the run-time rung (`POSITIONS.md:93`, "the 25-line value-position piece").
33	- **The thrown `bool`/`dim`/`unit` error** (`SkBoolMany`, `SkBoolCtl`, `SkBoolArm`). `SkBoolArm`'s pair is one the static-parameter sentence refuses, so refusing it is not a divergence in verdict from the committed specification. The limit itself, `bool` inference, is already gated by `XXXNatBoolChecker` (home 2). What remains is diagnostics: the error is placed at the declaration and hides the component's other errors, and the specification says nothing about diagnostics. **A note on row 307**, which stays open for `bool`, `dim` and `unit`: its claim already names those kinds (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:318`). No library declaration has a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` static parameter (a grep of `Library/*.fsi`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`), so the thrown form costs microGPT nothing. Rewriting it as an arm-level error is left for the rung that implements those kinds.
34	
35	## 4. Decision 3: it stands, and it goes to Pavol as the rung's decision
36	
37	The specification is silent on inference (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:15`). Pavol's rule gives the direction: an unknown size is an error only where it reaches a type, a name or a value (`POSITIONS.md:47`). But "a name" is ambiguous on the compiled path, where a call's static arguments name the instantiation. The candidates and their costs:
38	- **The rung's reading**: an unknown size at a call is the no-context error (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:247-249`). It is loud and reversible, and no other rung's file is touched. The costs: `SkDeadArm` is refused where walk and the type twin run, and compiled calls to the library's six vector `DOT` declarations need E3. The review's own E2 text already expects E3, because the fixed export checker "reports the extra parameter" of those six api declarations (`array-design-review.md:79`, `:181`). None of this is reached before the switch-over, because the compiled path does not read `FortressLibrary` until then (`POSITIONS.md:46`).
39	- **Sizes as types: a "bottom" size that reaches the instantiation name.** No size bottom exists. An `_InferenceVarInt` left in the static arguments trips the `OutAfterTypeChecking` assertion (`REPORT.md:56`), or it reaches `NamingCzar` and code generation, the run-time rung's files, where `CodeGen.java` is a stop for this rung (`CLIMB-BATCH-4.md:119`). And a dead size used as a value would then fail only at run time.
40	- **Default to 0.** This is E1, which Pavol did not take (`POSITIONS.md:47`).
41	- **A finer rule**: an error only when the arm's body or return type uses the size. It needs an analysis of the body that the checker does not have. It is larger than a repair round.
42	
43	I rule that the rung's reading stands. It is the loud side, it can be relaxed later without loss, and every alternative either needs files outside this rung or was declined. It is a decision taken under a silent specification, and it goes to Pavol as such, with (a), (b), (c) and the static-parameter point of section 2 item 1.
44	
45	## 5. What the worker got right
46	
47	The recorded failure, the count of 125 with crash row `none`, the provenance block, decisions 1, 2, 4 and 5, the precedent search for code, the specification derivation for the return-type rule, and the handling of `SubOvSwap` as the excepted shape with row 387. The skeptic verified each of these, and I found nothing against them in the diff. No stop file is touched: the diff's files outside `nodes/` and the rung's directory are the ones `REPORT.md:8` lists, and none of them is `compiler/StaticChecker.java`, `runtimeSystem/`, `compiler/runtimeValues/`, `CodeGen.java`, `OverloadSet.java`, `Library/` or `interpreter/`.
48	
49	## 6. The repair round, in order
50	
51	Work in `/home/user/fortress-nat` on `wip/rung-nat-checker` only, with the shell setup of the brief. Do not run `ant compileAll`, `ant testFast` or `ant testSystem`. `ProjectFortress/build` is current (`SKEPTIC.md`, inherited state), and nothing under `ProjectFortress/src/` changes. Run each `.test` in its own JVM, the way `probes/skeptic/junit-rerun.sh:6-10` does, and delete the test's entries under `default_repository/caches` before and after each run. Every new capture is a `.txt` file under `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/`, and its first line is the machine line (nproc, CPU model name and MHz, load average at start, JDK, `FORTRESS_THREADS`).
